mechanism_narrative: A higher federal funds rate directly increases the discount rate for equity valuation, leading to lower forward S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days. This relationship holds consistently across monetary policy cycles.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS exceeds 5.0% over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in unemployment rate below 4.0% signals a tight labor market that precedes inflationary pressures and monetary tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE remains below 4.0% over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS indicate aggressive monetary tightening against persistent inflation, compressing equity valuations and causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS fails to predict negative returns, with Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year period.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion, rising housing starts (HOUST) signal strong consumer demand and economic momentum, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when HOUST rises during late-cycle expansion over a 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Rising industrial production (INDPRO) indicates expanding supply capacity and economic growth, supporting corporate earnings and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO rises over a 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1) exceeds 2.0% annualized, it signals robust economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when GDPC1 growth rate exceeds 2.0% annualized over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Strong employment growth (PAYEMS) combined with high inflation (CPIAUCSL) indicates an overheating economy, prompting aggressive monetary tightening that results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising PAYEMS and CPIAUCSL fails to predict negative returns, with Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year period.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles, a rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) directly increases discount rates for equity valuation, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS rises during a monetary tightening cycle over a 3-year window.
